ajay: quick question — attempting to onboard lowland-7b (community release). License in the archive: `CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0` and README also has a note: "Weights may be redistributed for research purposes only; commercial hosting prohibited." Our quantization fork outputs `lowland-7b.q4_*` files. Can we: (a) host this in Redwood Hosted API for paying customers? (b) include quantized weights in Dedicated/reserved pools that serve customers? (c) bundle quantized weights in the on-prem installer for Enterprise customers? Need quick triage before folks run large evals.

olivia-legal: @ajay short answer: NC = non-commercial, SA = share-alike. Hosting on Redwood Hosted API for paying customers = not allowed. Dedicated pools that run for customers (where we operate infra and customers pay) = still commercial, so not allowed. Bundling/distributing quantized weights in our installer = redistribution -> likely disallowed. Safer alternative: provide BYO (bring-your-own) instructions so customers install their own copy in their VPC/on-prem and we do not distribute weights. :eyes:

maria-ml: follow-up: embeddings/feature vectors — if a customer runs lowland-7b in their Dedicated pool (we manage it for them under a contract) and we return embeddings to them for search/indexing, is that considered commercial use or a derivative work under CC-BY-NC-SA? Some of our product use-cases depend on embeddings.

olivia-legal: short but conservative: treat embeddings produced for paying customers as commercial use. CC-BY-NC-SA is ambiguous about "transformative outputs", but best practice is to block hosted/Dedicated commercial usage until counsel says otherwise. If the customer supplies weights and we never redistribute them (customer-managed VPC with customer-provided artifacts), that's a lower-risk path, but still requires per-customer legal check and explicit contract language. For public-facing deployments we should not use this model.

legal-bot: auto-triage: license_type=CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0; recommended_status=research-only; allowed_actions=["internal research/evals","non-commercial academic testbeds"]; disallowed_actions=["hosted commercial API","redistribute weights (including quantized)","bundle in installers"].

ajay: noted. Eng-ML wants to run internal quant benchmarks (latency/cost/quality) on our infra under an eval flag. That's internal and non-commercial — allowed, right? We'll avoid publishing numbers if legal prefers.

olivia-legal: internal benchmarking for product development/research is allowed under NC if not commercialized or offered to customers. Keep records of provenance and the license text. If we publish benchmarks or blog results, we must attribute upstream authors and clearly state NC/SA restrictions. Remember SA: if we modify weights and then redistribute derivatives, the derivative must be licensed under same terms — we cannot relicense quantized weights as proprietary.

sam-ops: small ops question: what exact blurb should appear in the model catalog so support and sales can see it? Need something <200 chars for UI.

olivia-legal: suggested blurb: "Lowland-7b (community) — CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0. Non-commercial use only. Hosting for paying customers and redistribution of weights (including quantized artifacts) is prohibited. Contact legal for enterprise exceptions."

maria-ml: plan: we'll tag the model `research-only` + `no-hosting` + `no-redistribute` in the catalog. Eng-ML will block pipelines that try to push it to hosted/dedicated deployers and expose BYO instructions for on-prem evaluation.

ajay: action items: @olivia-legal draft 1-pager + template clause for customer contracts; @maria-ml add model to catalog flagged research-only and add BYO docs; @sam-ops add the UI blurb. We'll gate any public benchmarks until legal gives go-ahead. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

olivia-legal: noted, will circulate draft by EOD. :memo:

ajay: closing thread — will kick off internal evals under strict "eval-only" tag and keep results internal. :lock:
